heisenberg_ricci.note: Generating directions have negative Ricci -b²/2; center direction has positive Ricci +b²/2.

product_obstruction.statement: For a PRODUCT g_B + eps^2 g_N with N = Heisenberg, Ric(e_1,e_1) = -b^2/2 but we need Ric >= (1-delta)eps^2. This requires b^2 <= -2(1-delta)eps^2 < 0, impossible for delta<1.
product_obstruction.conclusion: Products with nonabelian nilpotent fibers CANNOT have positive Ricci. The twist (A-tensor) is essential to compensate.
product_obstruction.key_point: For a SUBMERSION with twist A, fiber Ricci picks up |A_V|^2 >= 0, which can compensate -b^2/2. But this requires |A_V|^2 >= b^2/2 + (1-delta)eps^2.

abelian_forcing_scaling.fiber_Ricci_endomorphism: For eps-scaled fiber: Ric-endo = Ric^{g_N}(hat_e) / eps^2. For Heisenberg e_1: -b^2/(2 eps^2).
abelian_forcing_scaling.conclusion: b^2 <= 2|A|^2 (for small eps). If twist is bounded, b <= C. If twist = O(eps) (as in near-flat collapse), b <= C eps. In either case, b/eps -> 0 as eps -> 0, forcing abelian limit.
abelian_forcing_scaling.caveat: This argument assumes the collapsing sequence has local submersion structure. Under C^0 Ricci only, there is no general guarantee of this structure. The CZ spike shows C^0 Ricci doesn't control full curvature, so CFG-type fibration theorems don't directly apply.

product_abelian_obstruction.theorem: Products B x N with nonabelian nilpotent N have fiber directions with negative Ricci endomorphism. They cannot satisfy Ric >= (1-delta)g for delta < 1.
product_abelian_obstruction.proof: Milnor: Ric^{g_N}(e_gen) = -b^2/2 < 0 for generating e_gen. Product: Ric^g(e_gen)/g(e_gen) = -b^2/(2 eps^2) < 0.
product_abelian_obstruction.consequence: Nonabelian nilpotent collapse with positive Ricci REQUIRES twist (A-tensor). Products are excluded. This is clean and dimension-free.

summary.main_result: Product collapse with nonabelian nilpotent fiber is excluded by positive Ricci. For submersion collapse, bracket norm b satisfies b^2 <= 2(twist contribution) <= 2 eps^2 (1 + something bounded), forcing b = O(eps) -> 0. The fiber becomes abelian in the limit.
summary.missing: The passage from C^0 Ricci pinching to submersion structure with controlled twist. Under bounded sectional curvature (not available), this is CFG theory. Under C^0 Ricci only, this is the regularity gap.
summary.implication: If the regularity gap is closed, then tight positive pinching forces abelian collapse -> T^k determinant identity -> KK equations -> Einstein-Maxwell/Sasaki reduction. This is the all-dimensional positive-branch architecture.
